sources.title: Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Book 4, chapter 24 · Wilson translation
sources.edition: H. H. Wilson translation; narrative distinguished from translator footnotes
sources.locator: Nanda and Maurya transition, printed pp. 467–469

claims.subject: vp1112_satvata
claims.summary: The next chapter continues Satvata’s family under the Sātvata dossier.
claims.note: Editorial continuity link across adjacent chapters, not a newly narrated encounter. Both source-local nodes remain distinct; no identity resolution is inferred from spelling alone.

claims.subject: vp24_mahapadma_nanda
claims.summary: Mahāpadma Nanda is compared with Paraśurāma.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: A comparison in a future-king narrative; not a meeting, kinship, rebirth, or chronological synchronism.

claims.subject: vp24_kautilya
claims.summary: Kauṭilya is predicted to eliminate the Nandas’ dynasty.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: The passage’s object is the nine Nandas collectively. This edge points to their founder’s dossier and does not assert a particular personal killing method. It complements the existing Candragupta anointing claim GFD018.

claims.subject: vp24_mahapadma_nanda
claims.summary: Wilson’s translation also retains the Paraśurāma comparison.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: Another translation of the same work; not independent historical corroboration or another structural edge.

claims.subject: vp24_kautilya
claims.summary: Wilson also links Kauṭilya’s Nanda overthrow to Maurya rule.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: Textual prediction; narrative text only, without importing the nineteenth-century commentator’s historical chronology.

claims.subject: vp22_brihadbala
claims.summary: Chapter 22 resumes the Bṛhadbala lineage recorded in chapter 4.
claims.note: Continuity is inferred from the named lineage and the translator’s explicit cross-reference. Do not merge unrelated Gāndhāra or svayaṃvara Bṛhadbalas.

claims.subject: vp20_abhimanyu
claims.summary: Abhimanyu kills Bṛhadbala in the narrated Bhārata war.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: The named Abhimanyu is identified here as Arjuna’s son. This preserves the Viṣṇu Purāṇa witness without merging distinct epic namesakes.

claims.subject: vp24_pushpamitra
claims.summary: Puṣpamitra is predicted to kill his sovereign and take power.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: His sovereign is resolved contextually to the preceding final Maurya, Anubṛhadratha in this translation. Not the earlier Magadha Bṛhadratha or the later Puṣyamitra among the Mekalas.
